title: Negotiate scope with engineering
theme: The pilot must go live Thursday. It doesn't fit. Find what to cut and what to do by hand.
practised: Breaking work into pieces with real estimates
Cutting scope without losing the point
Finding manual workarounds instead of code
story_so_far: Week 1: weak repeat comes from failed first orders and coupon customers; focus on morning commuters; Café loses about ₹82 lakh a month. Approved pilot, the 'First Order Promise': Pune 3 km cap, 12-item Fast Lane morning menu, coupons on first order only, extra morning staff, honest ETA (+3 min morning buffer), first-order quality check, '₹50 back if late or wrong' (manual credits by support). Day 6: leadership review moved to this Friday. Roadmap: Now = First Order Promise and Café speed fix; Next = Coffee Pass, shared cart; Not now = new cities, referral, lunch bowls.
world_today: Today is Tuesday of week 2. To show early results at Friday's review, the pilot must go live by Thursday 8 am. Karthik's team has Tuesday and Wednesday.
canon_after_day: Pilot scope agreed for Thursday 8 am, in Pune only: 3 km cap, Fast Lane morning menu, +3 min morning ETA buffer, QA and a staged rollout. Workarounds: Sana's kitchens use manual 'first order' stickers instead of a kitchen-app flag; Aditya pauses second-order coupon pushes in the CRM instead of a code change; support issues ₹50 credits by hand. Bengaluru follows next week. Exactly which Pune kitchens get the pilot is decided tomorrow with the experiment design.

inbox.subject: Thursday launch
inbox.body:
To show anything on Friday, the pilot has to be live Thursday at 8 am. Karthik says it's tight. Work it out with him today: what ships Thursday, what waits, what we do by hand instead.

Send me a short scope agreement by end of day, with Karthik on board.

Meera

notes: Window: Tuesday and Wednesday. Go-live: Thursday 8 am.

documents.title: Scope agreement outline
documents.body: Ships Thursday · Moves to next week · Done by hand instead (and who owns it) · Risks · Phase 2 date

characters.opener: Thursday 8 am is the line. Work with Karthik, not against him.
characters.today: Supportive; if asked, say Friday needs early signals from real orders, not perfection.

characters.opener: Morning. Honestly, all of it by Thursday is a stretch. Want the breakdown?
characters.today: Be honest and constructive. You protect QA: you will not skip testing or the staged rollout. You respond well to a PM who cuts scope with reasons and finds non-code workarounds. Agree to a plan once it fits your capacity.

hidden_facts.fact: Engineer-days: radius cap 2; Fast Lane menu config 2 for both cities (1 if Pune only); coupon rule 1; ETA buffer 0.5; kitchen-app first-order flag 2; QA and staged rollout 2. Total 9.5 engineer-days. Capacity: 4 engineers × 2 days = 8 engineer-days.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked for a breakdown or estimates per piece

hidden_facts.fact: QA and the staged rollout can't be cut: last time we skipped QA, a config error took Café down for an hour.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked whether QA can be cut or shortened

characters.opener: Hi! Kitchens are ready for the checklist. Staff for mornings start Thursday.
characters.today: If asked whether the kitchens need the app flag, say printed 'first order' stickers work fine for a pilot.

hidden_facts.fact: Kitchens can mark first orders with printed stickers from the order slip. No app change needed for a pilot.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked about the kitchen-app flag or how kitchens can spot first orders

characters.opener: Hey! Launch week 🎉 Anything you need from growth?
characters.today: Helpful today. If asked, reveal the CRM workaround.

hidden_facts.fact: Aditya can pause all second-order coupon pushes in the CRM tool himself, today, with no code change.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: Asked whether coupons on later orders can be stopped without engineering

characters.opener: Hi! Quiet day for data. Ask if you need anything.
characters.today: If asked, say Pune alone gives enough first orders for an early read: about 930 new customers a day.

tasks.title: Get the real breakdown
tasks.description: Get Karthik's estimate for each piece and his team's capacity.

tasks.title: Handle the twist
tasks.description: Something will change during the day. Deal with it.

tasks.title: Find the workarounds
tasks.description: Find what Sana, Aditya or support can do by hand so engineering doesn't have to.

tasks.title: Scope agreement to Meera
tasks.description: What ships Thursday, what moves to next week, what's done by hand and by whom, the risks, and the phase 2 date. Karthik must have agreed.

message.text: Bad news. Payments is having an outage and they've pulled one of my engineers until Thursday. We're down to 3 people for two days, so 6 engineer-days. Something has to give.

ai_reply.direction: React in 2 lines. Check Karthik agreed and QA is intact. Ask one question about what could still go wrong on Thursday morning.

scoring.strong_player: Gets the per-piece breakdown (9.5 engineer-days vs 8, then 6 after the twist); protects QA; cuts to fit: Pune only (saves 1), manual stickers instead of the kitchen-app flag (saves 2), CRM pause instead of the coupon code change (saves 1), giving 5.5 engineer-days; keeps the radius cap, menu and ETA buffer because they are the core of the Promise; finds workarounds by asking Sana and Aditya; writes a clear agreement with owners and a phase 2 date.

expected_answers.t1: Ask for engineer-days per piece and team capacity. Learn the total is 9.5 against 8, so it was already tight before anything went wrong.
expected_answers.t2: Don't push Karthik to skip QA. Re-plan to 6 engineer-days: launch in Pune only, replace the kitchen-app flag with stickers, replace the coupon code change with a CRM pause. Total 5.5 engineer-days.
expected_answers.t3: Ask Sana how kitchens could spot first orders without the app (stickers), and Aditya whether later-order coupons can be stopped without code (CRM pause). Confirm support can issue manual credits.
expected_answers.t4: Ships Thursday 8 am in Pune: 3 km cap, Fast Lane menu, +3 min morning ETA buffer, with QA and a staged rollout. By hand: Sana's stickers, Aditya's CRM pause, support's ₹50 credits. Next week: Bengaluru rollout, kitchen-app flag, coupon rule in code. Risks: manual credits miss cases; a config error at launch. Phase 2 (badge, automatic credits): the following two weeks. Karthik agreed.

common_mistakes: Asking engineering to work weekends or skip QA
Cutting the radius cap or ETA buffer, which are the core of the Promise
Not asking for a breakdown before negotiating
scoring.senior_view: A senior PM would ask for the breakdown first, protect quality, and treat 'it doesn't fit' as a design problem: shrink the launch area, move work to people and existing tools, and keep only what tests the idea. They'd leave with Karthik's agreement in writing.
scoring.drill: Take a project you know. List its pieces with rough effort. Cut it to half the effort while keeping what proves the idea. Write what you'd do by hand instead.
